summary.name: Dimmerly
summary.one_liner: Dimmerly is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that controls brightness, warmth, and contrast separately for each display, including hardware DDC/CI control of external monitors.
use_cases: Dim an external monitor independently of the built-in screen
Warm the colour of each display in the evening
Recall a saved brightness and warmth preset for a whole desk
Schedule display changes at sunrise and sunset
Control a monitor's own brightness, contrast, volume, and input from the Mac
summary.what_it_does: Dimmerly runs in the macOS menu bar and sets brightness, warmth, and contrast for each connected display separately. For external monitors that support DDC/CI, it adjusts the monitor's own backlight, contrast, volume, mute, and input over the display cable. Monitors that do not respond to DDC/CI are dimmed in software instead. Users can save all display settings as a preset, apply presets on a clock or sunrise/sunset schedule, and trigger them via global shortcuts, desktop widgets, Shortcuts actions, or Control Center. Settings include display sleep or dim-only mode and an inactivity timer.
notable: Open source, listed in awesome-mac under Quality of Life Improvements
Hardware DDC/CI control of external monitor brightness, contrast, volume, mute, and input
Software dimming fallback for monitors that don't answer DDC/CI
Installable via Homebrew cask (brew install --cask dimmerly)
caveats: DDC/CI works best over a direct DisplayPort or USB-C cable; some docks, adapters, or HDMI ports may block it
Global shortcuts need Accessibility permission; sunrise/sunset schedules use location unless coordinates are entered
